qc_aile_ouest.blurb: Aile Ouest is a hard sport sector in the Sanatorium cliff complex in the Bras-du-Nord valley of Portneuf, reached by a trail above the main wall and a short metal ladder. Fourteen of its sixteen routes are bolted and two are trad. There is almost nothing easy here: the lines start around 5.10 and cluster in the 5.11 to 5.13 range, with the biggest group at 5.13. The wall stays in shade into the morning and then turns very hot under the sun, so it suits cooler days or early starts. Allow roughly twenty minutes of walking from the main wall.

qc_les_terrasses.blurb: Les Terrasses is the easternmost and main sector at Baie au Chene, on the Gaspe peninsula near Pointe-a-la-Croix. All sixteen routes are bolted sport lines on a vertical face roughly twenty metres tall at its highest. Grades are friendly for a regional crag: one at 5.8, a few 5.9s, then an even split between 5.10 and 5.11, so it works for solid intermediates more than beginners or hard-core projectors. The face points east, which gives sun in the morning and shade by afternoon. Reaching the base means a short but steep uphill trail from the car park.

qc_14_le_cosmodrome.blurb: Le Cosmodrome is a sector of the Lac Long cliffs near Saint-Alban in Portneuf, a venue whose ethic leans toward traditional climbing. Of its sixteen routes, ten are trad and six are sport, all on gneiss. The grade spread is steep: one route near 5.9, a handful at 5.10 and 5.11, and the bulk (eight) at 5.12, with one 5.13 at the top end. That makes it a sector for confident leaders rather than newcomers. Bring a full-range rack, since the trad lines take everything from small nuts and cams to larger pieces, and a 60 m rope is generally enough.

qc_04_la_cour.blurb: La Cour is a compact sector of the Lac Long cliffs near Saint-Alban in Portneuf, sitting beside the Roxanne and l'Arene sectors. It holds sixteen routes, fourteen of them trad and just two bolted, all on gneiss. The difficulty runs from one line near 5.9 up through 5.10 and 5.11 to a hard core of 5.12 and 5.13 climbs, with most of the best-rated ones in the 5.11 and 5.12 band. Expect to place your own gear on a full rack; the generally trad-minded Lac Long ethic applies here. A 60 m rope is enough for most of it, though some rappels can be tight.

qc_shawbridge.blurb: Shawbridge is a small ice and mixed venue in the Laurentians, about sixty kilometres north of Montreal and reached from a commercial car park by a walk along an old railroad bed. Sixteen routes are listed: fourteen ice and two mixed. The ice is mostly WI3 to WI5 with the most routes at WI5, and the two mixed lines are in the M7 to M8 range. Bring screws and slings for anchors, because there are few bolts, and two 60 m ropes if you want to set up long top-ropes. It draws crowds on winter weekends, so go midweek or early if you want the lines to yourself.
